newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eramet sees common ground in New Caledonia talks.
newsitem.headline: Eramet sees common ground in New Caledonia talks.

text.p: Eramet said Friday it found common ground with Falconbridge and Societe de Sud Pacifique (SMSP) in talks over a controversial plan to build a new nickel smelter in New Caledonia.

"A broad exchange of views enabled us to realise that the three establishments shared a common concern of carrying out, as quickly as possible, a study by SMSP and Falconbridge of this investment," Eramet said in a statement after a day of talks in Paris.

It said the three parties to the talks had agreed to each ask their experts to "study the technical, judicial and financial means of protecting their legitimate interests while resolving the problems identified during this meeting."
The goal, Eramet said, would be to enable a swap of mining assets between Eramet's Societe le Nickel and SMSP.
Under the plan Falconbridge and SMSP would get the right to use Eramet's Koniambo field to supply ore to their plant and Eramet would obtain the rights to the Poum field.

Eramet has repeatedly said it was supporting plans by Falconbridge and local Kanak company SMPS to build a nickel plant in the north of the South Pacific island as long as it did not threaten its development stategy in New Caleonia.
The French government supports the plan as it is part of a deal to appease local Kanak separists ahead of a 1998 referendum on independence for the island.
